No.19020/2025, which is first application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to appellant.

Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that it is a case of consensual relationship between two adults.

To support his contention, attention is drawn to the evidence of the mother of the victim (PW-1) who stated that her marriage was performed in the year 2004 and victim was born within one year of her marriage.

It is submitted that lady doctor, who had examined the victim i.e. Dr.
Akansha Verma (PW-11) had advised for ossification test for age determination, but there is no report of ossification test and, therefore, victim being a consenting adult as can be seen from the statement given by her to Dr. Akansha Verma (PW-11), it is evident that consensual relationship between two adults will not fall within the definition of rape as defined under Section 375 of IPC or 3/5 of POCSO Act.
3.
Ms. Shweta Yadav, learned Deputy Advocate General for the State in her turn submits that DNA report is positive and therefore, no indulgence is called for.

4. After hearing the learned counsel for the parties and going through the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:63508 3 CRA-7365-2024 record, we find that mother of the victim (PW-1)
stated that victim is her daughter.
She is aged about 17 years.
She was studying in Class-12th at Chapoora.
On 15th July, 2023 victim had gone to school when her younger sister returned back then they came to know that the victim was missing.
A report was lodged as contained in Ex.P/1 thereafter a missing person report was registered.
Spot map was prepared.
On 17th July, 2023 victim was recovered.
In para -5 of her cross-examination, this witness stated that her marriage was performed in the year 2004 and victim is her first child.
Victim was born within one year of their marriage.
5. Victim (PW-2) stated that she was studying in Class-11th.
She admitted that through-out her journey with the appellant she had never raised any alarm though there are several shops and other establishments on the way.
6. Father of the victim (PW-3), corroborated that his marriage was performed in the year 2004 and the victim is his first child.
7. Sheetal (PW-5) is the neighbourer of the victim and stated that she was studying in the same school in which this witness was studying.

In cross-examination this witness stated that when Akash had taken the victim then there were three students namely, victim, her sister and this witness PW-5 Akash vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133231174/
2 (Sheetal) present.

sentences.text: But none of them had opposed the victim's movement with the appellant nor they had raised any alarm and victim had left in the company of Akash, whereas this witness along with the younger sister of the victim had gone to their school.
8. Shri Ravindra Choudhary (PW-7) is the School Teacher.

He stated NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:63508 4 CRA-7365-2024 that in the school record (Ex.P/10) date of birth of the victim is mentioned as 10.07.2006.
In cross-examination he stated that date of birth of the victim was given orally by her parents and there is no documentary evidence in support of date of birth of the victim.
9. Dr. Akansha Verma (PW-11) stated in her examination-in-chief that on 08.07.2023 when she was posted as Medical Officer at District Hospital Burhanpur, victim was brought to her by constable.
She had taken permission of victim's mother for her internal examination.
Victim had informed her that Akash was studying with her in school and they were having affair.
Both ran away from their homes on their own volition and had established physical relationship on their own volition.
The lady doctor also stated that she had advised X-Ray of wrist and elbows for age determination.

But,
no X-Ray report is available on record.
10. Thus, it is evident that prosecution firstly did not produce Class-10th markesheet to prove the date of birth of the victim.
Secondly, Ex.P/11 'Dakhil Khariz' register is not supported with any documentary evidence to show the exact date of birth of the victim.

When statement of mother of the victim is taken into consideration, then she admitted that victim was born within one year of her marriage, which was performed in the year 2004, therefore, date of birth of the victim will be actually 10.07.2005 and the incident took place on 15.07.2023, when according to the lady doctor both the appellant and victim ran away on their own volition and had established physical relationship.

11. When these facts are taken into consideration, then failure of the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:63508 5 CRA-7365-2024 prosecution to get an ossification test done despite it being advised by Dr. Akansha Verma is fatal to the case of the prosecution as held by Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sunil Vs. State of Haryana [(2010) 1 SCC 742].

entities.text: Sunil Vs. State of Haryana [(2010) 1 SCC 742]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly, we have no hesitation to hold that as per the written testimony and the documentary evidence since the prosecution has failed to prove that the victim was minor at the time of incident, conviction cannot be sustained in the eyes of law.
12. In the result, Criminal Appeal is allowed.
Impugned judgment dated 31.05.2024, passed in SC No.36/2023 of conviction and sentence is set- aside.
13. Record of the trial Court be sent back immediately.

(VIVEK AGARWAL) (RAMKUMAR   JUDGE JUDG  Vin**
